newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guatemala guerrillas willing to restart peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala guerrillas willing to restart peace talks.

text.p: Leftist Guatemalan guerrillas said on Thursday they were willing to restart suspended peace talks aimed at ending Latin America's longest-running civil war.

The Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) said in a statement issued from its Mexico City offices that "acceptable conditions" have been created to return to negotiations with the government. Talks had broken off on Oct. 28.

The rebel statement appeared to have been coordinated with a government news release issued at the same time in Guatemala City saying that the government also has decided to renew talks with the guerrillas.
"President Alvaro Arzu has decided that indispensible political conditions exist for a return to the negotiating table," the government's Public Relations Ministry said.

Talks seeking an end to the 36-year-old war were called off after it was discovered that a rebel commando had kidnapped an elderly woman belonging to the family that owns Guatemala's largest cement company.
The URNG long has kidnapped people for ransom to finance its insurrection, but pledged to end such practices under preliminary agreements reached with the government.
